articles.title: Vino G. Bastian, Pevita Pearce, Faradina Mufti, Indra Jegel Lead ‘Miracle in Cell No. 7’ Director Lee Hwan-kyung’s Indonesian Father-Son Drama ‘Gasigogi’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Korean filmmaker Lee Hwan-kyung, director of “Miracle in Cell No. 7,” has assembled an Indonesian ensemble led by Vino G. Bastian, Pevita Pearce, Faradina Mufti and Indra Jegel for “Gasigogi,” a father-son drama now in production with Falcon Pictures.
body: The working title takes its inspiration from the stickleback fish. The male of the species remains alone with the eggs and fights off predators until his body gives out, at which point his flesh becomes the hatchlings’ first food. Lee uses the image as a metaphor for fatherhood and the sacrifices parents make for their children.

The project marks Lee’s return to directing following the success of the Indonesian version of his earlier phenomenon, and he has called it the most emotionally taxing film he has taken on. He made “Miracle in Cell No. 7” as a gift for his daughter. “Gasigogi” is dedicated to his son.

By shooting in Indonesia, Lee wants to draw on the country’s strong attachment to family, faith and community. He said the film is an original work rather than a transplant of Korean feeling, one that “breathes with Indonesian lungs.”

“Just as a father gives everything to his child, I want to pour everything I have into creating a precious gift for this family,” Lee said. “The name of that gift is ‘Gasigogi.’ The goal is simple: I want to create a film so honest and resonant that when the credits roll, the first thing the audience wants to do is call their father.”

articles.title: Kartik Aaryan’s ‘Captain India’ Set Amid Houthi Conflict in Yemen (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Kartik Aaryan’s upcoming action drama “Captain India” is set amid the Houthi conflict in Yemen, Variety understands. The film marks Aaryan’s first turn as a pilot. Shimit Amin directs the project, which is based on a real humanitarian evacuation. Aaryan’s character leads the rescue effort.
body: Kartik Aaryan ’s upcoming action drama “ Captain India ” is set amid the Houthi conflict in Yemen, Variety understands.

T-Series and Baweja Studios produce “Captain India” in association with Dopamine Studios, Aaryan’s banner. Bhushan Kumar of T-Series is among the producers, and S B Films handles production. Nash Vazifdar, Sanchit Gupta and Priyadarshee Shrivastava wrote the screenplay.

Aaryan most recently starred in “Tu Meri Main Tera Main Tera Tu Meri” and “Bhool Bhulaiyaa 3,” and has “Naagzilla” and other projects currently in the pipeline. Amin, meanwhile, is best known for directing “Chak De! India” and “Rocket Singh: Salesman of the Year” (2009), both for Yash Raj Films, and has largely stayed away from feature directing in the years since. He directed an episode of BBC/Netflix’s “A Suitable Boy” (2020).
The film is currently shooting in the U.K. “Captain India” will open in theaters on Aug. 13, 2027, over the Independence Day weekend in India.

articles.title: Ken Atchity, ‘The Meg’ Producer and Literary Agent, Dies at 82
articles.summary: Kenneth Atchity, “The Meg” producer and literary agent, died on Monday. He was 82. Across his career as a literary manager, producer and writer, Atchity produced more than 30 films; wrote over 20 books; negotiated publishing and entertainment deals; and published hundreds of additional titles…
body: Atchity also worked as a communication engineer at AT&T Long Lines, where he designed and implemented the Green Network, which connects NASA’s 26 research centers. He decided to change careers to produce “Shades of Love,” a set of 16 films which were broadcast on HBO and Cinemax and were internationally distributed by Warner Bros..

Born in Eunice, La., in 1944, Atchity was raised in Kansas City, Mo., and attended Georgetown University before entering Yale as a Woodrow Wilson Fellow, where he earned a masters in philosophy and a PhD. While there, his doctoral dissertation won the John Addison Porter prize, the university’s highest academic award, and was published with an introduction by novelist John Gardner.

Atchity is survived by his wife, Kayoko Mitsumatsu; his son, Vincent Atchity; his daughter, Rosemary Atchity; his five grandchildren, Margaret D. McKenna, Edward J. McKenna, Oliver D. Atchity, Eliot J. Atchity and Louis M. Atchity; and his sisters, Mary Calhoun and Laurie Dressman..
Donations may be made to Yoga Gives Back, an organization empowering women and children in India which Atchity served on the board for.

articles.title: Strictly's new presenters - after frosty reviews have they warmed up?
articles.summary: Josh Widdicombe, Emma Willis and Johannes Radebe have split opinion but are getting into the groove, critics say.
body: Strictly Come Dancing's new hosting trio received a very mixed reception when the latest series began a month ago. Ratings have dipped and the jury's still out, but critics say they are slowly getting into the groove.
Changing the hosting team on the BBC's flagship Saturday night entertainment show was never likely to be a waltz in the park.
And going from two presenters to three, and giving them slightly different roles, upset the show's rhythm even more.
Tess Daly and Claudia Winkleman were always going to be a hard act to follow.

articles.title: I expect you to cry: what the James Bond actors may face at the final audition
articles.summary: Jack Lowden, Callum Turner and Josh O’Connor are rumoured to be the final candidates taking screentests this weekend. So how can they best prepare? And who is likely to triumph? This weekend, the identity of the next James Bond is finally expected to be known – to the insiders, at least.
body: To say it has been a long time coming is an understatement. It is five years since Daniel Craig was killed in a hail of missiles at the end of No Time to Die, and in that time – even long before it – a swarm of actors have been tipped to replace him, only to age out of the role due to a combination of indecisiveness and cutthroat backstage corporate shenanigans. Whoever is declared to be 007 will be joining the franchise after what is likely to be the longest fallow period in the franchise’s 64-year history.
As such, this is kind of a big weekend. Let’s run through what we know so far.

If three actors are to screen test for Bond this weekend, then they are Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor and Jack Lowden. If there are more – some outlets state that one other actor might be participating, others two – then they won’t include Jack O’Connell or Jacob Elordi, who are both out of the race for one reason or another.

The identity of the other actors are not yet known. Let’s take an uneducated guess and assume that one of them is a Beatle (the best fit is Harris Dickinson) and another one is more famous but less suitable (like Tom Cruise).

articles.title: Why Original X-Files Creator Chris Carter Didn't Read Ryan Coogler's Reboot [Exclusive]
articles.summary: Speaking to SlashFilm, original X-Files creator Chris Carter explained why he trusts Ryan Coogler and why he didn't get involved in his upcoming reboot series.
body: As the series' creator, Chris Carter has traditionally taken a large role in running "The X-Files" in the past. Yet during his tenure as showrunner, he gave many creative opportunities to a ton of writers and directors during the show's 11-season run. Some of those names include the likes of Glen Morgan and James Wong (who are responsible for creating the still-going "Final Destination" series) as well as Vince Gilligan. Yes, there may not have been a "Breaking Bad" or "Pluribus" were it not for "The X-Files."

"I mean, Ryan Coogler... he's amazing, and that he wants to take it on is amazing to me. It's a diverse cast, so it's his take on it. I'm curious to see where it goes. They sent me the script. I didn't read it because I want to sit and watch it like everyone else. I didn't want to have to think about it. I want to be entertained, and I know he's going to entertain me."
points: Speaking to SlashFilm, original X-Files creator Chris Carter explained why he trusts Ryan Coogler and why he didn't get involved in his upcoming reboot series.

articles.title: Why Cammy From Street Fighter (2026) Looks So Familiar
articles.summary: If you feel like you've seen the actress who plays Cammy in 2026's Street Fighter somewhere before, we can help you solve that mystery.
body: Fans of Capcom's "Street Fighter" video game series know that the character of Cammy first appeared in 1993's "Super Street Fighter II: The New Challengers," a spin-off of the immensely popular "Street Fighter II" arcade game from 1991. Cammy is the character with the long blonde braids, the thong bodysuit, the painted-on leg camouflage, and the beret. According to that game's lore, she belonged to a special forces outfit called Delta Red.

In the 1994 "Street Fighter" movie, Cammy was played by Australian pop star Kylie Minogue, but in Kitao Sakurai's new "Street Fighter" film, Cammy is played by Thai-born Australian actress Mel Jarnson. "Street Fighter" proved to be Jarnson's second major fight-based video game role, as she had already played the villainous character of Nitara in Simon McQuoid's lackluster 2021 film "Mortal Kombat." She didn't return for "Mortal Kombat II," as the bat-winged Nitara was killed by Kung Lao (Max Huang).

articles.title: ‘Fighting an impossible fight is the only way to reclaim dignity’: Lee Chang-dong on class warfare and his searing Oscar contender
articles.summary: The auteur’s new film – a study of labour, capital and the fallout of redundancy – won the grand jury prize at Venice. Telling tales of the disenfranchised is ‘our moral responsibility’, he says. A quintessential 21st-century horror story: a private equity firm has set its sights on your company.
body: In 2009, workers at Ssangyong Motors company protested against plans to lay off between 37 and 43% of the workforce, staging a historic 77-day strike and occupation of the factory that was eventually broken up by riot police. “Until that point in time in Korea, labourers’ rights were widely accepted,” Lee says, speaking through an interpreter in a central London hotel; “however, afterwards, the basic rights of labourers changed; to the public, they couldn’t be seen as more important than market profitability or corporate competitiveness.”

At the time, Lee shelved the project. “The more I examined the pain of these individuals” – after the violent crackdown on the Ssangyong Motors strike, there were several suicides, and reports of long-term mental health issues – “I constantly asked myself: am I worthy of telling this story? And if I am, how do I tell it? Do I stand close to the workers, or keep my distance?” Later he and his co-writer Oh Jung-mi, wrote “many different” scripts, including one with post-apocalyptic elements, before Oh suggested introducing a character who is a documentary film-maker, thereby finding a way to work in Lee’s ambivalence about his intentions.
